market_name: Will 6 Fed rate cuts happen in 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the probability move is corroborated by front-end rate futures (SOFR/Fed funds futures) and 2Y yield; confirm it isn't isolated noise in a thin Polymarket book.
time_plan.1h: Compare TLT/yield direction against the prediction-market shift; look for any macro headline (CPI, jobs, Fed speak) that already explains it (already-public risk).
time_plan.2h: Assess persistence: is the yield move holding or mean-reverting? Re-check dollar and gold for confirmation of a coherent dovish theme.
time_plan.6h: Evaluate whether US session price action confirmed the dovish signal or faded it; note magnitude vs the modest expected band.
time_plan.12h: Final read: did TLT close higher with lower yields? Log realized vs predicted and whether the prediction market led or lagged public data.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of 6 rate cuts (150bps of easing) in 2026 signals a materially more dovish rate path than currently priced. Lower expected policy rates compress the front end and pull down the whole curve, boosting long-duration bond prices. TLT is the most direct, liquid duration proxy. A dovish repricing of this magnitude in the prediction market would map to falling yields.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Confirm the prediction-market move and check if DXY is weakening and real yields (TIPS) are falling in tandem.
time_plan.1h: Distinguish a rate-driven gold move from a risk-off/geopolitical driver, which would change the interpretation.
time_plan.2h: Check gold's correlation with the dollar and Treasuries this session for a consistent dovish narrative.
time_plan.6h: Reassess whether gold held gains; watch for reversal if rate-cut pricing fades.
time_plan.12h: Final read on GLD close vs prediction; note if move was rate-driven or dominated by other factors.

predictions.reasoning: A dovish shift toward 6 cuts implies lower real yields and a weaker dollar, both supportive of gold. GLD is a liquid proxy that responds to falling rate expectations. The mapping is looser than for Treasuries since gold also carries a large geopolitical/safe-haven component, so confidence is lower.

evidence_used: Market question implies a very dovish scenario: 6 cuts = ~150bps of easing in 2026
Rate-cut expectations map directly to Treasury yields, the dollar, and gold via real-rate and discount-rate channels
Liquid ETF proxies (TLT, GLD) capture duration and real-yield sensitivity
uncertainty_notes: Direction of the prediction-market move is assumed to be a rising probability of many cuts (dovish); a falling probability would flip all signs
Polymarket rate-cut markets can be thin and driven by a few traders rather than genuine information
12h moves in these ETFs are typically tens of bps, far below the 700bps tradable threshold — so no prediction is tradable
The market's tagged topic 'military_conflict' appears mislabeled; treated as a pure monetary-policy market

llm_justification.summary: This market tracks whether the Fed delivers 6 (150bps) of cuts in 2026 — a deeply dovish outcome. If its implied probability rises sharply, the coherent public-market read is a dovish rate repricing: long Treasuries (TLT) up as yields fall, and gold (GLD) up on lower real yields and a softer dollar. Both mappings are plausible but modest in a 12h window, well below the 700bps tradable bar, so this is research-only with moderate confidence. Treasuries are the cleaner proxy; gold is noisier due to safe-haven cross-currents.
key_assumptions: The observed anomaly is a rise, not a fall, in the probability of many cuts
The move reflects genuine dovish rate-path information, not book noise
No offsetting macro shock (e.g., inflation surprise) dominates the tape
failure_modes: The probability move reverses quickly as thin-market noise, and yields/gold don't follow
The dovish shift was already public (driven by a released CPI/jobs print or Fed speech), so no leakage edge exists
Gold moves for geopolitical/safe-haven reasons unrelated to rates, breaking the mapping
A risk-on equity rally accompanies the dovish move and steepens the curve, muting or reversing the long-bond gain
Sign error: the market actually reprices toward fewer cuts, in which case TLT and GLD fall
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
